_comment: Who may sign in to the LCDash cloud pilot. This file is the record; run
scripts/sync_cognito_users.py to make Cognito match it.
Roles (see app/core/cloud_pilot_roles.py):
user          - restricted; the tier the sanitized build narrows
supervisor    - UNRESTRICTED read access, including live CAD with patient
and reporter PII
admin         - supervisor access plus pilot access review
No role grants CAD write access, dispatch, paging, or any operational
output. That boundary is enforced in code, not here.
DELIBERATE DECISION, Ted Sparks, 2026-08-08: every current account is set to
supervisor because this group is the pilot test cohort, including staff from
two vendors (nga911.com, css-mindshare.com) and three outside agencies
(boonewv.com, e911.org, leasa.org). Ted was shown that supervisor means
unrestricted access to live CAD including patient and reporter PII, and chose
it knowingly so these testers can exercise the real product. He intends to
remove them after testing. Revisit when the sanitized 'user' tier exists --
the non-county accounts here are the ones it was conceived for.
ted@911logan.com was added 2026-08-08 as a second admin to exercise the full
new-account path end to end: administrator-created invite, first-time password
set, then MFA by emailed code. tedsparks@911logan.com was already CONFIRMED
with a password from 2026-08-05, so it can only test the returning-user half
of the flow, not the invite half.
ROLE HISTORY, ted@911logan.com: moved admin->supervisor on 2026-08-09 to be
the second role in the two-role identity verification (two accounts had to
resolve to DIFFERENT roles to prove the verifier reads claims). Moved back
supervisor->admin later the same day BY THE ADMIN PAGE ITSELF -- that role
change was the page's live verification, and taking effect at next sign-in
completed it. As of 2026-08-09 the POOL is authoritative for runtime role
changes and this file is the trailing record; when they disagree, the pool
is right and this file should be updated to match, not the reverse.
The 'name' values below are placeholders taken verbatim from each email's
local part. Real names were not on the Cognito accounts and have not been
guessed; replace them as they become known.
Removing someone from this list disables their account on the next run;
it does not delete it, so the account remains available for audit.
